title: Price Discrimination Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 25
description:
A college student picks up a Laddoo Lab six-pack, sees Rs 120, and puts it back. She loves the taste, but she cannot spend that much. Should Zoya lose her, or charge her a different price? In this animated lesson we follow Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, to understand price discrimination.

You will see what price discrimination means (the same product sold to different buyers at different prices, even though it costs the same to make) and a live run of one week at the stall: with one price for everyone, 50 parents buy and 20 students walk away (Rs 6,000); with a Rs 100 student price on a college ID, everyone buys (Rs 8,000), and each student pack still earns Rs 20 over its Rs 80 cost. We check the four conditions that make it work, then walk through the three degrees of price discrimination described by economist Arthur Pigou in 1920, with examples from a car dealer, a wholesaler and a museum. We also look at the human side honestly: more people can afford the product, but those who pay more can feel cheated, secret personal prices feel unfair, and India's Competition Act, 2002 bans unfair or discriminatory prices by a dominant firm. All figures are example figures.

This is Episode 25 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
